says: Hello! I am Pip. Let us count five red apples into my basket.
picture: A sunny playroom with pale yellow walls and a light wooden floor, seen straight on from the front at Pip's height; bright even daytime light. Left to right: a tall wooden shelf of coloured blocks stands against the back wall on the left; a round red rug lies in the middle of the floor; on the rug, Pip stands on the left side of the rug, whole body seen from the front, facing the viewer; a wide shallow light brown woven basket sits on the rug to Pip's right, empty, its low rim turned so the whole inside of the basket is seen; five red apples lie in a row across the right half of the red rug, each apple fully visible and touching nothing else; a big round window with blue sky behind Pip on the right. Pip is one sky-blue ball body with one grey ribbed antenna curving to the viewer's right tipped with a yellow ball, two very big round white eyes with black pupils, two dark blue eyebrows, a tiny smiling mouth, a small grey disc on each side, a grey band with three round yellow buttons, two short grey ribbed arms with sky-blue mitten hands, and one dark grey rubber wheel on a grey fork. Pip's left mitten hand is raised beside the body in a wave; the right mitten hand is empty and open at Pip's side.
does: Pip's raised left mitten hand swings gently side to side on 'Hello'. On 'Pip' the hand lowers to Pip's side and the body tips forward in a small bow, then straightens. On 'five' the right mitten hand lifts and sweeps slowly along the row of five red apples on the red rug, left to right, without touching them. On 'basket' the same mitten hand turns and points at the empty light brown woven basket. The antenna with its yellow ball sways once after the point. The five red apples stay in their row on the rug and the basket stays empty. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing disappears. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Pip closes the mouth and smiles.

says: In goes one. In goes two.
picture: A sunny playroom with pale yellow walls and a light wooden floor, seen straight on from the front at Pip's height; bright even daytime light. Left to right: a tall wooden shelf of coloured blocks stands against the back wall on the left; a round red rug lies in the middle of the floor; on the rug, Pip stands on the left side of the rug, whole body seen from the front, leaning a little to the right; a wide shallow light brown woven basket sits on the rug to Pip's right, empty, its low rim turned so the whole inside of the basket is seen; four red apples lie in a row across the right half of the red rug, each apple fully visible; a big round window with blue sky behind Pip on the right. Pip is one sky-blue ball body with one grey ribbed antenna curving to the viewer's right tipped with a yellow ball, two very big round white eyes with black pupils, two dark blue eyebrows, a tiny smiling mouth, a small grey disc on each side, a grey band with three round yellow buttons, two short grey ribbed arms with sky-blue mitten hands, and one dark grey rubber wheel on a grey fork. Pip's right mitten hand is held up above the red rug, halfway between Pip and the basket, holding one red apple on top of the open mitten, the whole apple and the whole mitten hand in clear view; the left mitten hand rests at Pip's side.
does: On 'In goes one' the right mitten hand carries the held red apple slowly through the air the whole way from above the red rug across to over the light brown woven basket, lowers into the basket, and the apple rolls off the mitten and comes to rest on the floor of the basket, still fully in view; the mitten hand lifts out empty. The eyes follow the apple down. On 'In goes' the same mitten hand travels back down to the red rug, closes under the nearest red apple of the row of four and lifts it up, so three red apples are left in the row. On 'two' the mitten hand carries that apple the whole way across to over the basket and lowers it in beside the first apple; both red apples lie in the basket in clear view, and the mitten hand lifts out empty. The antenna with its yellow ball bobs once. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing disappears. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Pip closes the mouth and smiles.

says: Three apples. Four apples. Five apples.
picture: A sunny playroom with pale yellow walls and a light wooden floor, seen straight on from the front at Pip's height; bright even daytime light. Left to right: a tall wooden shelf of coloured blocks stands against the back wall on the left; a round red rug lies in the middle of the floor; on the rug, Pip stands on the left side of the rug, whole body seen from the front, leaning a little to the right; a wide shallow light brown woven basket sits on the rug to Pip's right with two red apples lying side by side on the floor of the basket, both apples fully visible over its low rim; two red apples lie in a row on the right half of the red rug, each fully visible; a big round window with blue sky behind Pip on the right. Pip is one sky-blue ball body with one grey ribbed antenna curving to the viewer's right tipped with a yellow ball, two very big round white eyes with black pupils, two dark blue eyebrows, a tiny smiling mouth, a small grey disc on each side, a grey band with three round yellow buttons, two short grey ribbed arms with sky-blue mitten hands, and one dark grey rubber wheel on a grey fork. Pip's right mitten hand is held up above the red rug between Pip and the basket, holding one red apple on top of the open mitten, the whole apple and the whole mitten hand in clear view; the left mitten hand rests at Pip's side.
does: On 'Three apples' the right mitten hand carries the held red apple slowly the whole way through the air from above the red rug across to over the light brown woven basket and lowers it in beside the two red apples already there; three red apples now lie in the basket in clear view and the mitten hand lifts out empty. On 'Four' the same mitten hand travels back down to the red rug, lifts one of the two red apples from the row, carries it the whole way across and lowers it into the basket on 'apples'; four red apples lie in the basket. On 'Five' the mitten hand travels down to the red rug once more, lifts the last red apple, carries it the whole way across and lowers it into the basket on 'apples'; five red apples lie in the basket in clear view and the red rug is left bare. The eyes look down into the basket each time and the antenna with its yellow ball bobs with each apple. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing disappears. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Pip closes the mouth and smiles.

says: Five red apples all in my basket. Well counted! Goodbye for now!
picture: A sunny playroom with pale yellow walls and a light wooden floor, seen straight on from the front at Pip's height; bright even daytime light. Left to right: a tall wooden shelf of coloured blocks stands against the back wall on the left; a round red rug lies in the middle of the floor, bare apart from the basket; on the rug, Pip stands on the left side of the rug, whole body seen from the front, facing the viewer, standing straight; a wide shallow light brown woven basket sits on the rug to Pip's right holding five red apples resting together on its floor, every apple fully visible over the low rim; a big round window with blue sky behind Pip on the right. Pip is one sky-blue ball body with one grey ribbed antenna curving to the viewer's right tipped with a yellow ball, two very big round white eyes with black pupils, two dark blue eyebrows, a tiny smiling mouth, a small grey disc on each side, a grey band with three round yellow buttons, two short grey ribbed arms with sky-blue mitten hands, and one dark grey rubber wheel on a grey fork. Both mitten hands are empty and open at Pip's sides.
does: On 'Five red apples' the right mitten hand lifts and moves slowly above the light brown woven basket, passing over the five red apples without touching them, all five staying in clear view in the basket. On 'basket' the same mitten hand points down at the basket and holds there. On 'Well counted' Pip's body gives one small happy bounce on the dark grey rubber wheel and the antenna with its yellow ball springs once. On 'Goodbye' the right mitten hand rises beside the body and swings gently side to side, and keeps waving to the end. The five red apples stay in the basket and the red rug stays bare. Nothing appears from nowhere and nothing disappears. The mouth opens and closes with every word. After the last word Pip closes the mouth and smiles.
